html:
The Temple of Literature, Văn Miếu, is a temple to Confucius in Hanoi, founded in 1070 by Emperor Lý Thánh Tông of the Lý dynasty. In 1076 it became home to the Imperial Academy, Vietnam's first national university.

The academy at first taught the sons of the royal family and nobles, and later talented commoners, who studied the Confucian classics in Chinese characters for the state exams. Vietnam's rulers borrowed this model of government by scholar officials from China while defending their independence from it.

In 1484 Emperor Lê Thánh Tông began setting up stone tablets carved with the names of those who passed the highest imperial examination. Eighty two survive, each standing on the back of a stone turtle. They list doctors from 1442 to 1779.

The academy moved to the new capital at Huế in 1803 under the Nguyễn dynasty. The temple, with its five courtyards, remains one of Hanoi's best known sights, and students still visit before exams to pray for luck.
